newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-THREE SENT OFF AS HAMBURG SEND CELTIC CRASHING OUT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-THREE SENT OFF AS HAMBURG SEND CELTIC CRASHING OUT.

text.p: Three men were sent off -- two from Celtic and one from Hamburg -- as an ill-tempered UEFA Cup return match erupted in violence at Hamburg's Volsparkstadion on Tuesday night.

Hamburg won the match 2-0 to advance to the third round 4-0 on aggregate but their victory was overshadowed by the first-half dismissals of Celtic's Malky Mackay and John Hughes who were booked twice by Belarus refree Viktor Schuk.
He also sent off Hamburg's Markus Schupp in the 71st minute for a second bookable offence.
As well as the dismissals Celtic lost their leading scorer, Portuguese striker Jorge Cadete after only 13 minutes when he was carried off after a vicious foul by Hamburg defender Stephane Henchoz.

Celtic manager Tommy Burns had a furious on-the-pitch argument with the referee as the teams disappeared into the dressing room at halftime. Just before the interval, following Hughes's red card there were ugly scenes involving a dozen players in the centre circle.

First half goals from Karsten Baron (24th) and Andre Breitenreiter (50th) gave the Germans victory and meant that Celtic, who became the first British side to win the European Cup back in 1967, maintained their recent woeful showing in Europe.
It is now 13 years since they have reached the second round of any competition.
Germans Schalke 04 also advanced to the next round. They had no problems beating Roda Kerkrade 5-2 on aggregate after drawing 2-2 on the night.
An early strike by Schalke's David Wagner dashed Dutch hopes that Roda JC could overturn a 3-0 first leg deficit.
After just 15 minutes Wagner slotted into an empty net after Martin Max intercepted a back header by Roda defender Richard Roelofsen.
Roda, needing five goals to win the tie, scored 10 minutes later through Edwin Vurens but Schalke's Belgian striker Marc Wilmots made it 2-1 in the 72nd minute.
Two minutes later Gerald Sibon pulled one back for Roda with a shot from an acute angle but Schalke were destined to continue their first European excursion for 19 years.
In Prague, headed goals by Martin Penicka and Robert Vagner in the opening half hour set Slavia Prague on their way to a 3-1 win over Malmo and a 5-2 aggregate victory.

Jens Fjellstrom pulled back a goal in the 56th minute but any hopes of a storming finish by the Swedish side were snuffed out when Pavel Horvath converted a 69th minute penalty after Jiri Vavra had been pulled down by Tommy Jonsson.
Two teams scraped through on the away goals rule -- Boavista of Portugal and Casino Graz of Austria.
Boavista lost 2-1 at home to Odense but drew 4-4 on aggregate and went through because they scored three times in Denmark. Graz, who lost 3-1 to Germinal Ekeren of Belgium won 2-0 at home to qualify.
